title: Gazpacho
subtitle: Chilled Andalusian tomato and vegetable soup
excerpt: Spain's great chilled soup: ripe tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, garlic, and bread blended with olive oil and sherry vinegar into a smooth, vividly red liquid that is cold, sharp, and intensely flavoured. Served ice cold in summer with chopped garnishes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gazpacho originated in Andalusia in southern Spain and has been eaten in the region for centuries; early versions predate the arrival of tomatoes from the Americas and used bread, oil, vinegar, garlic, and water. The tomato-based version now considered classic emerged after tomatoes became established in European cooking in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The dish is defined by its technique: all the ingredients are raw and uncooked, blended and then chilled, so their freshness is paramount. The best gazpacho requires excellent ripe tomatoes; out-of-season pale tomatoes produce a flat, watery result. Sherry vinegar, traditional in Andalusia, gives the correct sour note; red wine vinegar can substitute.

content.text: Use the ripest tomatoes available; this is a summer dish. Blend until completely smooth, then pass through a fine sieve for a silky result. Chill for at least 2 hours before serving; the flavours develop and the soup must be very cold. Season after chilling, as cold mutes saltiness.

items.preparation: stale; white; soaked in water for 5 minutes and squeezed out

content.text: Put the tomatoes, pepper, garlic, soaked bread, and a pinch of salt in a blender. Blend on high speed for 2 minutes until smooth. With the motor running, pour in the olive oil in a thin stream. Add the vinegar and blend briefly.
Pass through a fine sieve, pressing to extract as much liquid as possible. Discard the solids. Taste and adjust salt and vinegar. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until very cold.
Taste again after chilling and adjust the seasoning. Serve in chilled bowls or glasses with the diced tomatoes and diced pepper scattered on top, a drizzle of extra olive oil, and bread on the side.
